messages.content:
Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: benefit
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation reduced depression severity (BDI-II) more than placebo in patients with mild to moderate depression.
Sentence: "At the end point, statistically significant changes were observed only in intervention group as compared with controls including increased 25(OH)D concentration (+ 40.83 ± 28.57 vs. + 5.14 ± 23.44 nmol L-1, P < 0.001) and decreased depression severity (-11.75 ± 6.40 vs. -3.61 ± 10.40, P = 0.003)."
Measured as: depression severity (Beck Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 56 patients aged 18-60 years with mild to moderate depression
Intervention: cholecalciferol 50,000 IU every 2 weeks for 8 weeks
Comparator: placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 56
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

content.text: {"rationale":"Study A's improvement was a single-arm before-after change in a combination supplement, while Study B was a placebo-controlled trial of vitamin D alone, so the two don't really conflict.","verdict":"apparent","reason":"design_or_bias","also_differs":["population","intervention","comparator","outcome_measure"],"detail":"Study A is an uncontrolled case series with no comparator, so its before-after change cannot show an effect; the 'harm' label seems to be a misread of a score that increased in the direction of improvement"}
